reasoning: Set A is the more rigorous quant plan. It has purged and embargoed folds, EWMA/GARCH/HAR baselines with QLIKE, placebo, planted-signal and simulated-GARCH harness checks, a single-use holdout for each stage, hand-built solvers checked against references, and the null-hypothesis-testing skill named at every test. All six stages are specified down to testable requirements. But A is about 3,000 lines and carries a lot of residue from being built up incrementally. Its spec still lists 'Machine-learning portfolio methods' and 'deep learning' as out of scope, which contradicts stages 5 and 6. PPO has 'six sleeves', but only five are listed and the architecture's SLEEVES list has five. The architecture overview and AD-20 still describe one or two holdouts where there are now three. The idea files keep superseded holdout dates and diff-style 'How it fits' notes. The brief's success criteria cover only stage 1. Set B is a quarter of the length, internally coherent and easy to follow. It has one shared evaluation protocol: an AsOfView leakage guard, one locked 3-year holdout that every stage respects, trades at the next day's close, delisting-return sensitivity checks, and an append-only ledger. It routes every chance claim to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name (TEST-01, plus COV-05, PORT-05, FEAT-04, FCST-04, VERD-03 and PAPER-04). B is thinner and weaker on quant points: no candidate feature list, volatility baselines with no HAR or GARCH, no purge, a data source that knowingly fails DATA-03 for delistings before 2018, and a CVXPY runtime minimum-variance solver. Even so, its consistency, right-sizing and structure outweigh A's extra rigor under this rubric.

strengths: Every stage is specified with concrete, testable acceptance criteria and real-world examples (Lehman, Tesla's addition, Apple splits, FB to META)

Strong anti-self-deception machinery: harness calibration with noise features, planted signals, relabelling, simulated GARCH, perfect-foresight and random allocators, a hash-chained log of tries with Holm correction, and single-use holdouts

Quant choices are sound: Ledoit-Wolf, a fitted Marchenko-Pastur edge, HRP with the original column-distance step, purged/embargoed walk-forward, QLIKE with EWMA/GARCH/HAR baselines, Grinold-style IC x vol x z expected returns, and a PPO sleeve allocator trained on bootstrapped histories
Fits the learn-by-building goal: hand-written estimators, solvers, a NumPy network and PPO, each checked against a reference in tests only
Names the null-hypothesis-testing skill at every test step (WALK-08, SCREEN-02, INCR-05, FCMP-02, TCMP-03, HOLD-03, PAPER-04) and in a matching AD for each study
Budget is concrete and within limits (Tiingo $30 plus a $15 GPU cap)
weaknesses: Very long (spec 751 lines, architecture 1,020 lines, eight idea files) for a terse solo developer
Heavy residue from incremental edits: '(changed 2026-10-15)' markers, a superseded AD-19 stub, and idea files full of 'Changes X / removes Y' diffs
Several contradictions: out-of-scope lines vs stages 5 and 6, six vs five sleeves, stale holdout ranges in the architecture overview and idea files, AD-20 still saying two holdouts
The brief's success criteria and problem statement frame only stage 1
The stage-2/3 study reads every year through the latest month, which breaks the holdout rule that no study reads 2026 data before the trading unlock
No explicit build order or 'start here'; next steps have to be dug out of very long documents

strengths: Compact and coherent; brief, spec and architecture agree, with no stale text and no history residue

One shared evaluation protocol (calendar, costs, cap, eligibility) and one locked holdout used by every stage, enforced in the loader with an AsOfView and HoldoutToken plus a poisoned-future fuzz test
Clean hand-off to the skill: code never decides significance, TestSpec plus inputs go to the null-hypothesis-testing skill, which is named at each test step
Careful backtest realism: execution at the next day's close, delisting returns bracketed at -30% and 0%, and a cost grid of 0/10/25 bps
The final verdict requires beating all three frozen classical benchmarks on both Sharpe and variance, with beat/lose/inconclusive outcomes
Ordered CLI (ingest, build, validate, eda, stage2, ...) and a component table that points dependencies downward make the build order clear
weaknesses: Stage 4 names no candidate features anywhere, and the FPORT spec is thin
Volatility forecasting is judged only against trailing-average and EWMA baselines; there is no HAR or GARCH
No purge or embargo is specified for walk-forward folds with 21-day labels, and there is no harness calibration with placebo or planted signals
The chosen data vendor knowingly lacks splits and dividends for names delisted before 2018, which conflicts with DATA-03 for the 2008 leavers
Minimum variance and the forecast-driven optimizer use CVXPY at runtime, against the persona's wish to build core methods first and compare to libraries later
A stock-level PPO trained on about 200 monthly decisions has a high risk of overfitting (acknowledged in the risks)
